The word marquee has two distinct core meanings — one tied to a large tent, the other to a sign above a building. Both are in widespread use today, but they belong to slightly different contexts. Here's each one explained fully.
Meaning 1: A Large Tent for Events

A marquee is a large, often elegant tent that is set up outdoors to host an event — a wedding reception, a corporate gathering, a garden party, a festival, and so on. It is not a small camping tent. Think of it as a temporary, portable hall made of fabric and supported by poles, big enough to fit dozens or even hundreds of guests, usually with decorated interiors, lighting, flooring, and furniture arranged inside.

This use is especially common in British and South Asian English, as well as in Australia and parts of Europe.

Examples:

  • "The wedding reception was held in a marquee on the lawn of the estate."
  • "They had to quickly move under the marquee when it started raining."
  • "The company hired a marquee for the annual outdoor gala."

The key idea here is that a marquee is a grand, purpose-built temporary structure — not a random tent you'd find at a campsite. It signals occasion, scale, and often a degree of formality or festivity.
Meaning 2: The Signboard Above a Theater or Venue Entrance

In American English, a marquee is the large, often illuminated sign or canopy structure that projects over the entrance of a theater, cinema, hotel, casino, or similar venue. It typically displays the name of the current show, the film being screened, the featured performers, or the name of the establishment itself, often in big, bold lettering — and traditionally, with lightbulbs around it.

When you picture a classic Broadway theater from the outside, the thing overhead at the entrance — displaying the show's title and lead actors' names in large letters, sometimes framed in lights — that is the marquee.

Examples:

  • "Her name was up on the marquee for the first time after years of hard work."
  • "The marquee outside the cinema read: 'Now Showing: One Last Ride.'"
  • "Hundreds of fans gathered outside the theater under the marquee."

Having your name "on the marquee" is a mark of stardom — it means you are being publicly advertised as the main attraction. This leads directly to the figurative use below.
The Figurative Extension: "Marquee" as a Noun Meaning a Star or Highlight

Because the marquee sign traditionally displays only the most important names and acts — the headliners — the word has evolved to describe someone or something that is the biggest draw, the most prominent feature, or the defining highlight of something.

When used this way, "marquee" functions as a noun that means the headline attraction or the biggest name in a lineup.

Examples:

  • "She's the marquee of this year's film festival." (= the biggest name / the centerpiece attraction)
  • "The team signed him as their marquee ahead of the new season." (= their star signing, the player who headlines everything)

This figurative use is closely tied to sports, entertainment, and business, where the concept of a "headline act" is common. It can also appear as a modifier — "a marquee player," "a marquee event" — meaning top-tier, headline-level, or of standout significance. But even in those cases, the root concept being drawn from is the noun: the idea of the theater marquee that only displays the biggest names.
Meaning 3: In Computing and Web Design (a more technical context)

There is a third, more technical meaning used in computing. A marquee refers to a piece of text or an image that scrolls automatically across a screen, usually horizontally — mimicking the way text or names scroll across a physical marquee sign (like the ones on hotel facades or news tickers). This was a feature in early web design, implemented via the HTML <marquee> tag.

Example:

  • "The website had a marquee at the top showing the latest announcements scrolling across the screen."

This use is now considered outdated in web design, but the word still appears in legacy code and in discussions of design history.

The word marquee always involves something prominent, visible, and meant to be noticed — whether it's a grand tent that dominates a venue, a blazing sign above a theater entrance, a celebrated name displayed for all to see, or scrolling text drawing the eye. The common thread across all meanings is display, scale, and importance. When something is described as a marquee — in any form — it is always the thing that stands out, the thing that announces itself.
